minutes.headline: Commission continued Unitil's large Mass Ave substation expansion pending a DEP number and a wetland-mitigation choice.
minutes.summary: The Conservation Commission approved several routine wetlands orders (60 Cross Road stormwater basin, 922 Flat Hill Road house, a Crocker Ave wall, a Johnson Street compliance certificate, a Sunset Lane tree determination) and continued others, including Unitil's proposed substation expansion at 934 Mass Ave, which drew extended discussion over wetland replication options. Much of the second half of the meeting concerned the town's long-vacant custodial property (Palace/Hollister Road), including unpaid bills, possible unauthorized entry, needed repairs, and next steps toward finding a new custodian.

budget_items.what_was_said: A member cited the current balance of the custodial property's account and noted the commission used to receive a monthly amount from the custodian, which has not been added to since the custodian left.

budget_items.topic: Proposed annual town appropriation to a conservation fund
budget_items.what_was_said: The open space committee reported an idea, from the planning director's prior community, of asking the town for a small annual appropriation into a conservation fund to pay for land appraisals ahead of potential land trust grant applications.

The stormwater subcommittee reported reviewing updated GIS impervious-area data for commercial properties in town as a step toward developing a stormwater utility fee, to be discussed further at the next meeting.

decisions.decision: The commission indicated it wants Unitil to pursue both wetland replication options for the 934 Mass Ave substation project — restoring the former abandoned substation site and additional buffer-zone planting — rather than choosing only one.
The conservation agent will proactively notify permit holders that orders of conditions are valid for three years, prompting them to request extensions or certificates of compliance before lapsing.
The conservation agent will add the town's unfinished third batch of encroachment cases to a list to revisit, after checking with the former chair about existing files.
The commission will ask the town's legal counsel for a standardized template tenant/custodial agreement for the vacant Palace/Hollister Road property, rather than an open-ended request for input.
A commissioner (Mary) will contact a cleaning company (e.g., ServPro) for a cleaning/repair estimate on the vacant custodial property before the commission commits any funds.

what_happened.line: Unitil's proposed substation expansion at 934 Mass Ave was continued to June 3, pending a DEP file number.
The commission wants Unitil to pursue both wetland-mitigation options -- restoring the old substation site and added buffer planting -- rather than pick one.
Extended discussion of the town's vacant custodial property (Palace/Hollister Road) covered unpaid bills, possible unauthorized entry, and needed repairs, with no resolution reached.
The commission will ask town counsel for a standard tenant/custodial agreement template before the property is used again.
The stormwater subcommittee reported reviewing updated GIS impervious-area data as a step toward a possible stormwater utility fee.

why_it_matters: The substation expansion is a wetlands permit for utility infrastructure near Mass Ave; its scope and mitigation depend on the June 3 continuation.
The custodial property is town-owned and has sat vacant and accruing bills; how it is reused or leased affects the commission's small budget.
A stormwater utility fee, still in an early data-gathering stage, could eventually become a new charge tied to a property's paved or built-over area.

reconciliation.summary: The two records agree on nine of the ten votes we recorded, all unanimous, and on most attendee names once caption errors are resolved.
